new_statements.quote: Transcriptions of data are adapted to IPA standards, with the following exceptions. The letter ‹y› is used for the palatal glide [j], Tarangan mid-close [e] and [o] are transcribed ‹ê› and ‹ô› (mid-open [ɛ] and [ɔ] are transcribed ‹ɛ› and ‹ɔ›), and unexpected stress is marked by an acute accent. (The normal pattern is penultimate stress, or final stress if the final syllable contains a mid-vowel.)
new_statements.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press (langsci 526).
new_statements.locator: Grimes & Edwards 2026, ch. 6 Aru, p.273 (also sec. 2, pp.87-88 quoting Nivens 2017)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: group-level-statement. On-disk text (boan1242/ lines 14267-14272, p.273; lines 5764-5770, pp.87-88) shows the sentence is Nivens (2017)'s transcription convention for the whole comparative Aru dataset ('the normal pattern is penultimate stress, or final stress if the final syllable contains a mid-vowel'), relayed secondhand, not a description of Lola; Lola rows carry several acute-marked 'unexpected stress' forms (ŋamá, ʔanáwi, menayá), so Lola-specific placement is not established beyond the Aru default. | checker: Grimes & Edwards 2026 (langsci 526) full text held by the project (boan1242/): ch. 6 'Aru' opens p.273 with the transcription note (the text layernext page mark…
new_statements.relation_note: States that for the Aru data the normal (unmarked) pattern is penultimate stress, or final stress if the final syllable contains a mid vowel; deviations carry an acute accent (e.g. Barakai gamár, ʤágel, da-bálar).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word stress penultimate; final if the last syllable has a mid vowel (e/o); other placements lexical and marked with an acute in the data.
new_statements.exceptions: final stress when the final syllable contains a mid vowel; individually marked words with acute accent
new_statements.identity_note: group-level statement: a transcription convention stated for all Aru data in the chapter (Nivens 2017 database, Hughes/Daigle/Schapper field lists); Lola is one of the Aru languages tabulated (map Fig. 6.1, tables 6.x). [name in source: Lola; pages ch. 6 'Aru', p.273 (transcription conventions, from Nivens 2017; restated pp.87-88); Lola forms in Tables 6.x; map Fig. 6.1 (Lola, Warabal)]

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. (comp.). Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: 'Lola' (Maluku, Indonesia). Data: Jock Hughes, SIL International, 22 February 1997, taken from SIL linguistic survey list. Leipzig: MPI-EVA (lingweb).
sources.note: No statement, but the numerals are transcribed WITH stress marks (apostrophe before the stressed syllable): 1 ye'tu, 2 ro, 3 'lasi, 4 'kaha, 5 'lima, 6 'dubu, 7 dubu'yam ('6+1'), 8 ka'ro ('2x4'), 9 'seri, 10 ka'ɸi, 100 'ratu('ie), 1000 riɸn'e. Penultimate stress in 8 of the 10 marked polysyllables, final in ye'tu and dubu'yam (the latter a compound). Wordlist-only data; the compilers logged this page as silent, which is correct for statements but it does carry first-hand stress marking by Hughes.
